judgments.reasoning_cat1: The coverage grant lists specific liability lines and conditions cover on underlying insurance affording 'limits not less than' the Schedule, which is largely mechanical, though 'excess liability policies' and 'Heliport Liability' are undefined.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It is expressly deleted and replaced by Amendment No. 4 (c070) for policies effective on or after October 1, 1996, so its temporal reach relative to Amendment No. 4 and the Stipulation of Termination (c099) could be argued.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A schedule of numeric underlying limits; the only softness is 'each medical incident' versus 'each occurrence' terminology across lines.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Amendment No. 4 (c071) adds duplicate nursing home/outpatient entries and Article III (c076) deems each claim an occurrence, which sits awkwardly with 'each medical incident' here.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Subject to the provision that a separate Limit of liability may apply' is permissive and unattributed — it is unclear whose policy provision governs or who decides, a genuine latent ambiguity.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It must be read with Article XI's run-off sentence (c033) continuing discovery/extended reporting coverage after cancellation and with the Rating Schedule-B claim-conversion endorsement at no cost (c086), which raises questions about premium for the extra limit.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A one-line incorporation of attached clauses with nothing to construe on its face.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The incorporated Nuclear Incident Exclusion Clause No. 1 is a physical damage form and Clause No. 2 refers to homeowners and family auto policies, which fit poorly with an excess hospital liability treaty.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Teaching hospital', 'children's hospital' and 'psychiatric hospital' are undefined and boundary-vague (many general hospitals have teaching programs), and 'loss arising out of the operation by the insured' invites argument.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Amendment No. 1 (c053) deletes this and narrows it to 'operation of a teaching hospital' for post-July 1995 policies, and the rating schedules charge for occupied psychiatric beds, which cuts against a psychiatric exclusion.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The defined term is 'total beds' but the definition counts 'occupied' acute care beds alongside 'all bassinets' and other categories, a mismatch that leaves the count genuinely uncertain.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Amendment No. 1 (c054) substitutes a 350-bed threshold with the identical definition, and the Rating Schedule's occupied-bed-equivalent counting (c050) uses a different measure of beds.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Arising out of the ownership, operation or use of helicopters owned or leased by the insured hospital' is standard causation language, though 'arising out of' always has some reach.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Article I (c001) expressly grants Heliport Liability cover, so the line between an excluded owned/leased helicopter loss and covered heliport liability is a real internal tension.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A closed list of named counties; definite and easily applied.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Amendment No. 1 (c055) replaces it, dropping Cuyahoga County while Rating Schedule-A (c061) creates a Territory 3 rate for Cleveland, which is coherent but shows the lists move together.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Any pool, syndicate, association, insolvency fund, guaranty fund or other combination of insurers or reinsurers' is a classic catch-all after enumerated specifics, squarely raising ejusdem generis.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It overlaps with Nuclear Incident Exclusion Clause No. 1(1) and No. 2(1) (c034, c043) covering pools and associations, which is duplicative rather than contradictory.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Reinsurance assumed by the REINSURED' is a short, standard and well-understood exclusion.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It sits consistently with the Offset article (c032) which contemplates the parties acting as assuming reinsurer or ceding company under other treaties.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Business to the extent that it is reinsured outside of this agreement' is vague as to what 'reinsured outside' captures (facultative, other treaties, self-insured retentions) with no definition.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Article III (c012) contemplates a self-insured underlying hospital professional layer and the Offset article (c032) contemplates other treaties between the same parties, so the scope of this exclusion interacts with both.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The retention formula is dense and the figures are internally garbled ('$93,000,000' where $9,000,000 is meant), which is the kind of mechanical slip that changes meaning.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It is superseded twice, by Amendment No. 1 (c056, $25,000,000) and Amendment No. 4 (c076), leaving three versions whose temporal application must be reconciled.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The definition mixes 'actually paid' amounts with 90% of extra-contractual and punitive/exemplary awards conditioned on the CORPORATION having 'counseled with' and 'concurred in' the REINSURED's conduct — several undefined, contestable terms.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The insolvency proviso redefines loss as the amount 'incurred or is liable for' rather than paid, which pulls against the 'actually paid' core and against Article IX's reimbursement-on-proof-of-payment rule (c029).

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Net salvage, subrogation or any other recovery (after expenses)' uses a catch-all and an undefined expense netting, but the allocation formula itself is workable.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The Accounting Schedule credits 'all salvage received by the CORPORATION' to profits (c021), which must be squared with this recovery-sharing mechanic.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'All payments under the supplementary payments provisions ... including court costs, interest upon judgments, and allocated investigation, adjustment, and legal expenses' is an including-list whose reach beyond the enumerated items is uncertain, and 'allocated' is undefined.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It works with the express carve-out of claim expenses from 'loss' (c013), the pro-rata sharing in Article V (c017) and the salary exclusion (c016), all of which turn on this definition.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Two short, concrete carve-outs; 'statutory penalty' for unfair claim practice is reasonably determinate.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Article IV(c) (c013) brings 90% of punitive/exemplary damages arising from the REINSURED's claim conduct into 'loss', so the boundary with an excluded unfair-claim-practice penalty is contestable.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The proviso refers to claim expenses 'connected with such settlement or appeal' although no settlement is mentioned in the antecedent clause, an antecedent/mechanical slip, and 'benefit derived' is undefined.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Pro-rating by 'the amount of loss ultimately borne by the CORPORATION' interacts awkwardly with the 90% loss items in Article IV (c013) and with the retention split in Article III (c012/c076).

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A plain obligation to pay premium computed per the attached Rating Schedule and subject to its minimum premiums.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The Rating Schedule referenced is replaced twice (c057 Schedule-A, c077 Schedule-B), and the Schedule-B minimum premium figures ($1,000,000 and $1,500,000 per million) are on their face improbable.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A single sentence fixing a 25% ceding commission; nothing to construe.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It feeds the Accounting Schedule credit of premium 'net after ceding commission' (c021) and is consistent with it.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The operative first sentence is unreadable and the final accounting period is made to 'commence on the fifth January 1st preceding the termination date' although accounting periods are twenty-four months, an internal mechanical inconsistency.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Amendment No. 1 (c052) deletes only the first paragraph retroactively to 1994 while leaving these accounting-period mechanics, and c025 forbids any accounting period commencing after termination, so the run-off machinery is hard to reconcile.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The item numbering is corrupted and the charge for 'unpaid losses' plus 'losses paid during the accounting period attributable to claims occurring ... during the accounting period' leaves double-count questions.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Amendment No. 1 (c052) confines contingent commission to 'the first $1,000,000 of reinsured limits as respects each policy' but this schedule gives no method for allocating premium, losses or the 15% overhead charge to that layer.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Reserve of individual cases as developed to the date the computation is made' does not say who sets the reserves or whether IBNR is included, a real if narrow vagueness.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It drives the 'unpaid losses' charge in the Accounting Schedule (c021) and hence the contingent commission under c052, so a reserving dispute would ripple through.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A simple arithmetic definition of deficit carried forward as a charge.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It is consistent with the Accounting Schedule charge for 'the deficit, if any, at the end of the previous accounting period' (c021).

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Excess of credits over charges at the end of any accounting period' is arithmetic and definite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Amendment No. 1 (c052) speaks of 'net profit accruing to the REINSURED' limited to the first $1,000,000 of reinsured limits, which this whole-treaty definition does not accommodate.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The text is garbled and combines two rules — no accounting period commencing after termination, and no further commission until all premium is earned and all losses paid — whose relationship is unclear.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It sits uneasily with the annual re-computation obligation in Article VII (c020) and with the run-off contemplated by the termination article (c033) and the Stipulation of Termination (c099).

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Definite 20-day deadlines; 'a bordereau on a form satisfactory to the CORPORATION' gives one party a discretion but is a common formulation.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It coheres with the Accounting Schedule's reliance on 'written premium ... reported by the REINSURED' (c021) and with the offset right (c032).

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Prompt notice of any event or development which might result in a claim' is an open-textured trigger, and 'as may be requested' leaves the document duty indeterminate.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The Insolvency Clause (c047) restates the same investigate/settle/defend duty consistently, and Article IX's participation right (c028) fits alongside it.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'In the judgment of the CORPORATION' makes the trigger subjective but the right itself is narrow and expressly at the Corporation's own expense.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It is consistent with the reinsured's control of claims (c027) and with the reinsurer's separate defence rights on insolvency (c047).

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Promptly' and 'satisfactory evidence of payment' are undefined and give the paying party latitude, a modest but nameable vagueness.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The next paragraph (c030) contemplates the Corporation funding on the date the reinsured proposes to pay, which is in tension with requiring evidence that the loss has already been paid.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The sentence is mangled ('will furnish to the REINSURED the CORPORATION'S payment of loss ... on the date on which the REINSURED proposes to make payment'), leaving the obligation's content genuinely uncertain.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It pulls against the reimbursement-after-proof-of-payment rule in the preceding paragraph (c029) and against the definition of loss as amounts 'actually paid' (c013).

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A very short, broad grant — 'may inspect the records ... pertaining to the risks reinsured' — with no notice, time or scope limits, which leaves its boundary open.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Nothing else in the treaty limits or expands access rights, so it stands alone without conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Broad but conventional offset language; 'any balance' across other treaties is wide yet defined by category (premiums, commissions, loss, claim expenses).
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Offset rights collide notoriously with the Insolvency Clause's direction that reinsurance be paid to the liquidator without diminution (c046), a live internal tension here.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'In no event exceeding 12 months plus odd time' uses an undefined trade phrase, and 'in force prior to or as of the effective date in time of cancellation' is garbled, both nameable defects.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The Stipulation of Termination (c099) ends the treaty by reference to 'policies issued on or after January 1, 1998' rather than by the 90-day notice and run-off mechanism prescribed here.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Standard market nuclear pool exclusion; the wording is fixed-form and its terms are conventional.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It duplicates Article II(e)'s pool exclusion (c009) and Clause No. 2(1) (c043) without contradicting them.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A long enumerated physical-damage exclusion ending in a residual 'installations other than those listed ... using substantial quantities' catch-all, with 'substantial quantities' undefined here.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: This treaty reinsures excess liability coverages only, so a physical damage exclusion has no obvious field of operation under Article I (c001).

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The carve-outs turn on whether the 'REINSURED does not have knowledge' of the nuclear installation and on governmental approval, both fact-dependent and here textually corrupted.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Like the rest of Clause No. 1 it addresses property insurance, which does not map onto the liability coverages ceded under this treaty.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Named hazard specifically insured against' is a settled market formulation and narrow in scope.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It builds on paragraphs (1)-(3) of the same clause without inconsistency.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: It excepts risks where the nuclear exposure 'is not considered by the REINSURED to be the primary hazard' — a subjective, unmeasurable standard, and the paragraph is textually merged with the following definitions.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Its content is repeated as separate provisions (c039, c040) and it fits the property-oriented Clause No. 1 rather than this liability treaty.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A definition by reference to the Atomic Energy Act of 1954 and amendments; external but determinate.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It supports paragraph (2) of the same clause (c035) and conflicts with nothing else.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Making the REINSURED 'sole judge' of 'substantial quantities' and 'the extent of installation, plant or site' hands one party a discretion over an admittedly vague term.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It qualifies the residual limb of paragraph (2) (c035) and is otherwise self-contained.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A grandfathering provision keyed to policies issued before 31 December 1957, with garbled dates in this copy but a conventional structure.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The treaty was effective in 1994, so this transitional sub-paragraph has no realistic field of operation under Article I (c001).

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A Canadian-risk grandfathering provision, again date-keyed and form-standard.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The rating territories (c051, c060, c080) are all United States, so a Canadian transitional rule is inert rather than contradictory.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Standard nuclear association/membership exclusion with conventional wording.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It overlaps Article II(e) (c009) and Clause No. 1(1) (c034) without inconsistency.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The Limited Exclusion Provision is long and here badly corrupted, and its class list ends with 'policies of a similar nature' plus 'the liability portion of combination forms', a general-after-specific formulation.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The classes it addresses — family automobile, farmers comprehensive personal liability, homeowners — bear no relation to the hospital excess liability policies ceded under Article I (c001).

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The Broad Exclusion Provision enumerates specific liability coverages and the operative exclusion text is truncated in this copy, leaving what is 'deemed to include' incomplete.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Its list does include hospital-relevant lines (professional and malpractice, automobile), so unlike Clause No. 1 it can bite, but nothing else in the treaty addresses nuclear liability.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A statutory-form insolvency clause; its terms are prescribed and well settled, though it refers to New York Insurance Law for Ohio and Kansas parties.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The reference to Section 4118 of the New York Insurance Law fits neither party's domicile, and the clause's 'without diminution' rule is in tension with the broad offset right (c032).

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Standard statutory wording on the liquidator's assumption of the ceding company's duties and the reinsurer's right to interpose defences at its own expense.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It tracks Article IX (c027, c028) faithfully and does not disturb the definition of loss on insolvency in Article IV (c013).

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'A majority in interest' of reinsurers is undefined and the apportionment 'in accordance with the terms of this reinsurance agreement' has no obvious mechanism.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: This is a single-reinsurer treaty, so the multi-reinsurer premise has no counterpart elsewhere in the instrument, though the Article II(g) other-reinsurance exclusion (c011) contemplates parallel cover.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A conventional savings paragraph confirming the parties' status and disclaiming third-party rights.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It is consistent with the insolvency payment rule (c046) and with Article IV's insolvency proviso (c013).

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'CRNA's — each full-time equivalent x 5-10' gives a range rather than a rate with no rule for choosing within it, and the bassinet factor is rendered 'x 106', a plain figure error.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The same open range survives into Rating Schedule-A (c059) and Schedule-B (c079), and this schedule is deleted in full by Amendment No. 1 (c057) while Article VI (c018) still refers to 'the Rating Schedule'.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Territory 1 is defined as 'the remainder of the states of Ohio, Maryland, Kentucky, Illinois, Nebraska, Wyoming and Arizona not listed in Territories 2', so a risk in any unlisted state falls into no territory at all.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Rating Schedule-A (c060) and Amendment No. 2 (c066) rewrite the state list and add a Territory 3, and Article VI (c018) makes premium turn on whichever schedule is in force.
